lines.trans: Come in, please, here is our kitchen.
Regarding the hall, I have no complaints.
We strictly monitor cleanliness everywhere.
Now let's look at your kitchen carefully.
We have the best cooks working here.
I am interested only in sanitary rules.
All employees wear a clean uniform.
I myself will check every workstation.
Our head chef personally oversees everything.
In the kitchen one must not violate rules.
You can see everything yourself.
Then we begin a full sanitary inspection.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'everywhere' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Vanya, the water! There's water everywhere!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: И, Марина Сергеевна, читайте всё внимательно! Особенно мелким шрифтом!
examples.trans: And, Marina Sergeyevna, read everything carefully! Especially in fine print!
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Good deeds come back to the sender.
Understood. And who is managing the dining room?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Я тебя не интересую = you're not interested in me

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

контролировать.gloss: to control, to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to supervise, to keep an eye on, to control

examples.trans: I'm supposed to keep an eye on you!
Keep an eye on me right here!

examples.text: А слепые? Я же тебя контролировать должна!
examples.trans: What about the blind people? I'm supposed to keep an eye on you!
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: Anikeev came here in person, and what?

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание! Аникеев лично сюда приезжал, и что?
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building! Anikeev came here in person, and what?

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: на его место = in his place

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

examples.text: Тогда соблюдайте режим и не нарушайте.
examples.trans: Then observe the regime and do not violate it.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

related.gloss: intensified / related adverb (it is not allowed)

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice

examples.text: Плохой бетон привезли. Самсон, ты зря радиаторы носил.
examples.trans: They've delivered bad concrete. Samson, you carried those radiators for nothing.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.en: to come, arrive (idiomatic in добро пожаловать = welcome)

examples.text: Добро пожаловать в наш новый дом!

examples.trans: The guests arrived right at lunchtime.

examples.text: Очень приятно познакомиться. Добро пожаловать к нам!
examples.trans: Very nice to meet you. Welcome to our team!

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

examples.text: Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
examples.trans: All by the rules, like a knights' tournament.
Regarding the hall, there are no complaints.

examples.text: По залу у меня претензий нет.
examples.trans: Regarding the hall, I have no complaints.

examples.text: У вас есть претензии ко мне?
examples.trans: Do you have complaints against me?
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.en: to check, to test, to verify
meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to check, to test', paired with 'проверять'.

examples.text: Вот с таким настроением и иди к Аникееву. Паяльник проверь.
examples.trans: Go to Anikeev in just that mood. Check the soldering iron.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'check, inspection, test' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: An inspection is underway at the bank.

examples.text: Эксперты уже начали проверку состояния старой стены.
examples.trans: Experts have already begun checking the condition of the old wall.

пройти.gloss: to go through, to pass; to come along

meanings.note: about a feeling or pain: потом пройдёт = it'll pass
'Пройдёмте' = let's go, an official's polite order

проходить.gloss: to go through; to come in

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.en: sanitary, relating to public health or hygiene

examples.trans: A health inspector came to the restaurant.

examples.text: Сегодня пятнадцатое число, большая санитарная проверка!
examples.trans: Today is the fifteenth, a big sanitary inspection!

следить.gloss: to watch, to follow; to keep an eye on

meanings.en: to look after, to keep an eye on

examples.trans: Keep an eye on the child.
He is an experienced company employee.
Why are you mistreating our staff?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трого'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The teacher looked at us sternly.

examples.text: Нет, я нормально его пугал, строго!
examples.trans: No, I scared him properly, sternly!

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'uniform, form, shape' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The cook put on a clean uniform.

examples.text: Шеф, мне не выдали форму вовремя.
examples.trans: Chef, they did not issue my uniform on time.
All employees wear a clean uniform.

examples.text: У меня здесь всегда полная чистота.
examples.trans: I always have complete cleanliness here.
We must urgently establish perfect cleanliness.

examples.text: Да, шеф требует идеальной чистоты везде.
examples.trans: Yes, Chef demands perfect cleanliness everywhere.

meanings.note: short form чисто: всё чисто = everything is clean

examples.text: Нин, я всё помыл. Всё чисто.
examples.trans: Nina, I washed everything. It's all clean.

examples.text: Шеф-повар лично руководит работой на кухне.
examples.trans: The head chef personally oversees the work in the kitchen.
The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
